newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia said preparing rules for bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia said preparing rules for bank mergers.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank and the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) are preparing rules for mergers involving listed banks, the Jakarta Post reported on Thursday.
"The regulations are needed to prevent listed banks from being controlled by irresponsible people," central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono was quoted as saying.
Sudradjad said individuals or institutions could easily control the ownership of a bank by taking over a majority of a bank's shares.
Current regulations only cover the mergers of unlisted banks and are designed to encourage small banks to merge among themselves or with larger banks.
The government has issued a number of incentives to encourage such mergers, including tax facilities and an automatic promotion in status to that of a foreign exchange bank.
Sudradjad gave no indication when the new regulations would be announced.
